A statement said the surgery was “successful, on schedule and as planned”.The Vatican said Leo had “now returned to his room” after the operation. Entertainment.title: BEAMS Stitches Three Leathers Into One Broken-In Blouson
Entertainment.text: SummaryBEAMS’ new Leather Blouson combines sheep nappa, sheep nubuck and goat suede in a paneled constructionWashing, tumbling and hand-applied distressing give each jacket a worn-for-years look straight off the rackThe design draws on vintage sports jackets, reworked with a wide body and shortened lengthBEAMS has introduced the Leather Blouson as part of its Fall/Winter 2026 collection, a jacket built from three contrasting leathers and finished to look like a long-owned favorite. Offered in Soft Black and Taupe, the piece pairs a vintage sports jacket template with a contemporary wide, cropped silhouette.The jacket’s character starts with its materials, as BEAMS splices together three distinct hides across the body. Smooth sheep nappa and velvety sheep nubuck sit alongside goat suede, with the varying textures set against one another through bold paneling rather than blended into a single surface.Each jacket then goes through a multi-step aging process designed to replicate years of wear. Washing and tumbling break down the leather and draw out a faded tone, after which every piece is individually worked by hand to add the scuffs and highlights that typically form at stress points over time. Because the distressing is done one jacket at a time, the placement and intensity of the wear vary from piece to piece, along with the natural creases and color shifts inherent to the leather itself.Structurally, the blouson takes its cues from vintage sports jackets, updated with practical touches for daily use. Hand-warmer pockets sit at the front, each concealing a zippered security pocket inside, while ribbed trims finish the shape and a polyester lining keeps the interior smooth.BEAMS cuts the jacket in what it calls a Wide Short Fit, pairing a roomy chest with a deliberately shortened length. The boxy proportions give the piece a classic yet updated outline that works well over hoodies and heavier knits for layered looks.The BEAMS Leather Blouson is available now in Soft Black and Taupe via the BEAMS online store and at BEAMS locations in Japan.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: The MM6 Maison Margiela FW26 Campaign Is a Study in Motion and Normality
Entertainment.text: SummaryMM6 Maison Margiela unveils its FW26 campaign, photographed by Philippine Chaumont and Agathe Zaerpour.The collection reimagines everyday staples through unconventional proportions, exposed linings and unexpected styling.Highlights include tailored separates, sportswear, Bauletto bags and colorful concealing sunglasses.MM6 Maison Margiela has unveiled its Fall/Winter 2026 campaign, offering a fresh perspective on the collection's exploration of everyday dressing and exaggerated normality. Shot by Philippine Chaumont and Agathe Zaerpour, the new visuals revisit the themes established during the label's FW26 presentation at Milano Centrale, where the train station's constant movement of arrivals and departures served as a backdrop for a cast of familiar yet distinctly individual characters.Translating this concept into campaign form, the visuals place MM6's signature design philosophy of reduction, straightforwardness and reinterpreted wardrobe archetypes at the forefront. The collection challenges conventional ideas of ordinary clothing, finding unexpected character in familiar garments and proportions while maintaining the label's deliberately understated, offbeat sensibility.The FW26 wardrobe draws on recognizable staples, including checked shirts, denim jackets, tailored blazers, full skirts, tracksuit tops, ski sweaters and zip-up fleeces, reworked through subtle structural interventions and unconventional styling. Ribbed jersey back panels streamline the silhouettes of shirts, trench coats and jackets, while exposed linings, adjustable snap-fastened hems and reduced proportions introduce an element of experimentation. Styling further disrupts expectations, pairing sportswear with voluminous skirts and culottes, blazers with long johns, and oversized knitwear with tights.Accessories reinforce the collection's playful approach to the familiar, from Bauletto bags and brightly tinted versions of MM6's signature concealing sunglasses to earrings left attached to their retail display cards and rings missing their stones. The MM6 Maison Margiela FW26 collection is now available through the brand's official website and selected boutiques worldwide.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Spinnaker and seconde/seconde/’s New “50 Phantoms” Collaboration Reveals Its Ghosts Under UV Light
Entertainment.text: SummarySpinnaker and seconde/seconde/ return with a fourth “50 Phantoms” collaboration.“CRAZY” reveals its ghosts openly, while “QUIET” hides them until exposed to UV light.Both editions are releasing on October 16, priced at $600 USD.Spinnaker and French watch designer seconde/seconde/ are bringing back their cult “50 Phantoms” concept for a fourth annual collaboration, this time built around the Fleuss 40 Automatic. The 2026 edition turns the series into a literal game of hide-and-seek, placing 50 ghost figures throughout each watch and leaving their discovery to the wearer.Two personalities split the release: the openly playful “CRAZY” (SP-5195-11A) and the more restrained “QUIET” (SP-5195-11B). Both use a 40mm stainless-steel Fleuss case with a 47mm lug-to-lug measurement, screw-down crown and box-style sapphire crystal, while a polished white ceramic unidirectional bezel receives a custom wavy edge designed to recall the hem of a ghost’s robe.The difference lies largely in how each model handles its phantom population. "CRAZY" puts the concept front and center through a multi-layer white dial populated by printed and embossed ghosts in blue, white, green and yellow, distributed between the dial base and crystal and treated with luminous material for an especially animated appearance after dark. "QUIET" initially appears far more conventional, pairing a matte-white dial with applied silver indexes while hiding its ghost graphics until they are exposed to UV light. Swiss Super-LumiNova also appears across the hands, applied markers and bezel on both references.Power comes from a Miyota 9039 automatic movement, visible through the exhibition caseback, while 10 ATM of water resistance keeps the diver-inspired Fleuss platform intact. Each watch is supplied with a stainless-steel bracelet, orange nylon strap and white silicone strap - with the "CRAZY" version even cutting phantom silhouettes into its silicone strap -alongside a UV torch to uncover the concealed details.The presentation continues the joke beyond the wrist, with both watches arriving beneath a purpose-built glass ghost display dome surrounding a sculpted EVA-foam phantom, accompanied by a ghost-shaped cleaning cloth. The "CRAZY" edition is limited to 1,500 individually numbered pieces, while the subtler "QUIET" is capped at 850, with both priced at $600 USD.The Spinnaker x seconde/seconde/ Fleuss 40 Automatic “50 Phantoms” 2026 Edition launches on October 16, 2026, via Spinnaker, followed by a one-week pre-order period for an additional made-to-order production run determined by demand. Entertainment.title: Hermès’ New H08 Watches Play With Cool-Toned Ceramic
Entertainment.text: SummaryHermès expands the H08 with Bleu de Malte and Blanc Chantilly editions.Both 39mm models pair ceramic bezels with aluminum-coated glass-fibre composite cases.The H1837 automatic movement provides a 50-hour power reserve.Hermès is adding two fresh colorways to its contemporary sports-watch family with new H08 editions in Bleu de Malte and Blanc Chantilly.First introduced in 2021, the H08 has become one of the Maison’s most distinctive modern watch designs, defined by a cushion-shaped case that sits somewhere between a circle and a square, oversized graphic numerals and an emphasis on contrasting technical materials. The latest pair retains that familiar 39mm architecture, but shifts the character through cooler, lighter tones: both use a braided glass-fibre composite case coated with aluminum, framed by satin-brushed ceramic bezels with mirror-polished chamfers and finished with color-matched rubber straps.The Bleu de Malte version takes the sportier approach, pairing its blue ceramic bezel and rubber strap with a rhodium-plated, crystal-sandblasted dial. Applied ruthenium-plated Arabic numerals are filled with blue Super-LumiNova, while blue PVD-coated hands and a choice of orange or blue minute-track accents sharpen the contrast.Its Blanc Chantilly counterpart is considerably more tonal, using a white ceramic bezel, white lacquered dial and matching rubber strap to create an almost monochromatic treatment. Grey minute markings, ruthenium-plated numerals and black-gold hands add definition without disrupting the pared-back palette. Both retain the H08’s subtly offset date window at 4:30 and are water-resistant to 10 bar, keeping their cleaner aesthetic grounded in everyday practicality.Inside both watches is the automatic Hermès Manufacture H1837 caliber, a 193-component movement running at 4 Hz and delivering a 50-hour power reserve. Its finishing includes circular graining, snailing, satin-brushed bridges and an oscillating weight decorated with Hermès’ repeating “H” motif. For more information, head over to Hermès' official website.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

For a more textured, striking look, the “Bison” colorway offers a warm, earthy brown suede paired with soft yellow accents, while the "Molten Lava" execution turns up the volume in a vibrant red suede complete with contrasting laces. The shoe boasts a wider toe box, oversized eyelet rows, and chunky laces that give it a confident, heavy-set stance. Entertainment.title: ‘Attack on Titan: The Musical’ Heads to Singapore for World Tour Kickoff
Entertainment.text: SummaryAttack on Titan: The Musical begins its first world tour in Singapore in April 2027.The production runs at Marina Bay Sands from April 15 to May 2.Additional international tour cities will be announced later.Attack on Titan: The Musical has officially announced plans for an expansive world tour, which will kick off next spring in Singapore. Scheduled to run from April 15 to May 2, 2027, the highly anticipated stage adaptation of Hajime Isayama’s legendary manga will be hosted at the Sands Theatre within Marina Bay Sands. This initial engagement marks the original Japanese production's first-ever performance in Asia outside of its home country, following previous, highly successful, and completely sold-out runs in major cities like Osaka, Tokyo and New York.Presented entirely in Japanese with accompanying English subtitles, the production utilizes a specialized theatrical genre known as "2.5-dimensional theater," which seamlessly blends intricate costumes, complex choreography, high-tech stage effects, and detailed visual design to bring two-dimensional anime and manga properties to vivid life on a three-dimensional stage.Focusing heavily on the early chapters of Isayama's dystopian narrative, the musical adaptation is directed by Gō Ueki and features a book written by Masafumi Hata. The music, distinct from the iconic anime soundtrack, boasts original songs crafted specifically for the production under the guidance of music director and hip-hop artist KEN THE 390, alongside lyricist Kaori Miura. However, fans of the anime will be treated to at least one familiar auditory staple, as the beloved first-season opening theme, "Guren no Yumiya," is slated to be featured.The Singapore engagement is presented by Base Entertainment Asia, with general ticket sales having recently opened, signaling the start of a massive global rollout as the stage show prepares to announce further international tour dates in the near future.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

The researchers measured it in a layer of the semiconductor tungsten diselenide, just one atomic layer thick, using ultrashort laser pulses. Science & Technology.title: Apple’s HomePod mini 2 Just Joined Your Home Theater
Science & Technology.text: SummaryApple’s HomePod mini 2 pairs the S10 chip with computational audio that tunes playback to each track in real timeA new Sound Glow feature turns the speaker’s top into a reactive light canvas synced to bass, treble and album artThe speaker arrives in pink, green, blue, white and midnight, with Siri AI landing in a future software updateApple has unveiled HomePod mini 2, the second generation of its pocket-sized smart speaker, rebuilt around the S10 chip and a fresh five-color lineup. The update brings Sound Glow, a reactive lighting layer across the top surface, along with support for four-speaker surround sound, Mac speaker duty and the overhauled Siri AI assistant, which is set to arrive through a later software update.At the core of the speaker is the Apple S10 chip, which drives a computational audio system that reads music as it plays and adjusts dynamic range, loudness and acoustic output on the fly. The result is 360-degree sound from the same compact footprint, scalable from a single unit to a stereo pair or a full multiroom configuration.Sound Glow is the most visible addition, transforming the speaker’s top into a lit surface that pulses and shifts in real time with the low and high frequencies of a track. Colors are pulled from the album artwork in Now Playing, so each song generates its own palette, while ambient soundscapes such as rain trigger custom animations designed for winding down. Controlling Sound Glow by voice requires an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone.Those lighting effects play off the new finishes, offered in pink, green, blue, white and midnight and designed to coordinate with Apple’s Mac colorways. HomePod mini 2 can now act as the audio output for any Mac with Wi-Fi 6E or later, either solo or as a stereo pair, covering movies, games and video calls. “HomePod mini 2 brings together Siri AI, gorgeous new colors, and incredible audio,” said Kaiann Drance, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Home Product Marketing, in a press release.Home theater setups get a meaningful bump as well, since HomePod mini 2 can now form a four-speaker surround system with the 4th-generation Apple TV 4K. The speakers work out where each unit sits in the room and calibrate timing and levels automatically, with HomePod (2nd generation) also compatible provided the front and rear pairs match.Siri AI, built on an entirely new architecture using the latest Apple Foundation Models, will reach the speaker through a future software update in English across the U.S., Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa and the UK. Once live, HomePod mini 2 can distinguish up to six household members by voice and, when linked to an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, act on personal context across apps, from surfacing a song a friend texted to adding items to a grocery list. Households without a compatible phone still get Siri AI’s web-sourced world knowledge, more natural back-and-forth conversation and improved music discovery, while requests are processed either on-device or through Private Cloud Compute, where data is never stored or made accessible to Apple.As a smart home controller, the speaker handles voice-triggered routines like locking doors, closing the garage, dimming lights or adjusting the thermostat, and doubles as a home hub for remote control through the Home app. Sound Recognition listens for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms and pushes alerts to iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch, and the speaker can announce visitors by name via Face Recognition when paired with Apple Home Collection video doorbells and cameras, which roll out starting in December.Apple’s material spec extends to the internals, with fully recycled rare earth elements in every magnet and 100 percent recycled copper, gold plating and tin solder across all Apple-designed circuit boards. The packaging is entirely fiber-based.Pre-orders for HomePod mini 2 are open now via Apple and the Apple Store app across the US and more than 23 other countries and regions, with in-store availability beginning Friday, October 30. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Climate & Environment.text: Insurers are taking on more risk than they should. If – or when – a major disaster hits, the catastrophe will have far-reaching consequencesI work for a major insurer, assessing the risk posed by natural disasters on properties around the world, from family homes to schools, government offices and multibillion-dollar commercial centres. The world is facing greater risk than ever from extreme weather. We are not prepared – and that inaction could have profound consequences for the global financial system.In the face of ever more extreme and unpredictable climate risks, I am coming under pressure to cut my forecasts for the losses that disasters will cause in order to make insurance more affordable – and get my employer more business. In some instances, the questioning of our numbers and models is justified. But too often, it is not being done to produce more accurate models, but to artificially lower prices. If this is happening at my firm, which is struggling to compete with rivals’ prices, it’s happening elsewhere.The writer is a modeller working in the insurance industry. Art & Culture.title: 8 Must-See Art Shows and Installations During Frieze London 2026
Art & Culture.text: SummaryFrieze London 2026 brings a packed lineup of exhibitions, installations and performances across the city from October 14–18.Highlights include major presentations by Justin Caguiat, Tarek Atoui, Salman Toor and Issy Wood.Beyond traditional galleries, Slawn, JW Anderson and CART Department x Kozo blur the boundaries between contemporary art, fashion, design and public space.As Frieze London and Frieze Masters return to Regent's Park from October 14 to 18, the city's art scene is spilling well beyond the fairgrounds. Across London, major institutions, independent galleries and unconventional spaces are presenting a packed lineup of exhibitions, performances and installations.This year's highlights span everything from experimental sound and contemporary painting to large-scale interventions and collaborations at the intersection of art, fashion and design. Whether you're navigating the city between fair visits or looking to skip the tents altogether, here are standout presentations worth checking out during Frieze Week.Justin Caguiat, ‘Change Ringing’ at Serpentine SouthOctober 8, 2026 – January 10, 2027Justin Caguiat makes his UK institutional debut with ‘Change Ringing,’ an ambitious exhibition spanning painting, sculpture, printmaking, sound and film. Taking over Serpentine South, the presentation explores the relationship between art, architecture and the passage of time. Among the highlights are paintings made with heat-sensitive pigments that shift in color and appearance depending on their environment, alongside bronze bells cast in the forms of flowers and seeds. The result is an evolving exhibition that challenges the idea of an artwork as something fixed.Tarek Atoui, ‘Hold’ at Tate ModernOctober 13, 2026 – April 11, 2027Lebanese artist and composer Tarek Atoui transforms Tate Modern's iconic Turbine Hall into an expansive sonic environment for the latest Hyundai Commission. Titled ‘Hold,’ the installation brings together custom-built instruments, sculptural objects, electronics and percussion to create an evolving orchestra of sound and movement. Visitors are invited to experience the work through both listening and physical sensation, while a program of live performances will continually reshape the space. It's a monumental exploration of how music, architecture and human interaction can exist as one.CART Department x Kozo, ‘A World Within’ at The Peninsula LondonOctober 15–31, 2026 | The Peninsula LondonCART Department and The Peninsula London have teamed up with artist Kozo to transform six of the hotel's luxury vehicles into moving works of art. Titled ‘A World Within,’ the project sees Kozo bring his intricate visual language to a fleet of Rolls-Royces, Bentleys and other vehicles, drawing inspiration from London's rich cultural history, British nature and surrealist imagery. Blending elements of the past, present and future, each vehicle becomes a canvas for the artist's fantastical world, where familiar motifs take on unexpected forms. Unveiled during Frieze Week, the fleet will travel throughout London in October, bringing contemporary art off the gallery walls and onto the city's streets.Slawn, ‘Crane Painting’ with Saatchi YatesOctober 13, 2026 | Doon Street Car ParkNever one to follow the traditional gallery playbook, Nigerian-born, London-based artist Slawn takes his practice to an industrial scale with a special painting performance presented with Saatchi Yates. Staged at the Doon Street Car Park, the intervention brings together cranes, cars and the artist's unmistakable visual language, turning an everyday urban setting into an unconventional canvas. Known for bridging street culture, contemporary art and spectacle, Slawn continues to challenge where and how art can be experienced.JW Anderson, ‘A Composition’ in PimlicoOctober 15–20, 2026Jonathan Anderson brings together art, fashion and design for ‘A Composition,’ a special exhibition presented by JW Anderson in partnership with The Platinum Card by American Express. Taking place at the brand's Pimlico flagship, the presentation features new works by Cerith Wyn Evans alongside contributions from artists and makers within Anderson's creative circle. Highlights include ceramics by Akiko Hirai, paintings by Mary Stephenson and sculptures by Shawanda Corbett. The exhibition offers a closer look at Anderson's long-standing dialogue with contemporary art and craftsmanship, extending his creative vision beyond clothing and into the gallery space.Salman Toor, ‘Someone Like You’ at The Courtauld GalleryOctober 2, 2026 – January 10, 2027Salman Toor's first solo exhibition in Europe arrives at The Courtauld Gallery with ‘Someone Like You,’ bringing together 19 paintings created since 2019. Known for his atmospheric depictions of contemporary urban life, the Pakistani-American artist captures moments of friendship, desire, isolation and belonging through his signature palette of luminous greens and intimate interior scenes. Balancing tenderness with humor and unease, the exhibition offers a compelling look at how Toor navigates identity and human connection.Issy Wood, ‘Self-Portraits’ at the National Portrait GalleryOctober 9, 2026 – February 28, 2027British-American artist and musician Issy Wood turns the lens inward with a presentation of self-portraits at London's National Portrait Gallery. Created as part of the institution's Artist Focus series, the paintings explore intimacy, consumer culture and the complicated nature of self-representation. Through tightly cropped compositions, unusual perspectives and subtle distortions, Wood treats portraiture as a means of both revealing and concealing identity. The exhibition offers a more personal look at an artist whose practice moves fluidly between painting, music and contemporary culture.Rirkrit Tiravanija, ‘(situational awareness)’ at Pilar CorriasOctober 9 – November 14, 2026Rirkrit Tiravanija returns to Pilar Corrias with ‘(situational awareness),’ his fifth solo exhibition with the gallery. Presented at its Savile Row location, the show brings together new paintings and performance to examine the connections between British military history and the traditions of labor, craftsmanship and production associated with the famed tailoring district. Known for his socially engaged practice, Tiravanija approaches the gallery as a space for cultural exchange, drawing unexpected connections between historical narratives and the everyday rituals of making.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Acne Studios and Hussein Chalayan Reimagine Archival Designs in New Collaboration
Art & Culture.text: SummaryAcne Studios collaborates with Hussein Chalayan on a 12-piece capsule inspired by his early 2000s collections.Highlights include patchworked denim, asymmetrical silhouettes and a reworked Camero handbag.An accompanying V&A campaign and limited-edition book celebrate Chalayan's creative legacy.Acne Studios has joined forces with British-Cypriot designer Hussein Chalayan for a 12-piece capsule that revisits some of his most influential designs from the early 2000s. Renowned for his conceptual approach to fashion, Chalayan helped redefine the boundaries of garment construction throughout the 1990s and beyond, treating clothing as a medium for exploring transformation, displacement, technology and the passage of time.Drawing inspiration from his SS01 "Ventriloquy", SS02 "Medea" and SS03 "Manifest Destiny" collections, the collaboration reinterprets his experimental design language through Acne Studios' signature materials of denim, jersey and leather. The partnership also reflects a creative dialogue between Chalayan and Acne Studios co-founder and creative director Jonny Johansson, whose shared interest in unconventional construction and material experimentation forms the foundation of the collection.Among the collection's highlights are patchworked denim jeans in Acne Studios' signature 1996 and 2009 fits, alongside a new twisted silhouette featuring a trompe l'oeil python print. A patchworked denim shirt, asymmetrical denim vest and dress reference the layered constructions of Chalayan's "Manifest Destiny" collection, with similar techniques extending into jersey T-shirts and vests. Accessories include a reworked Camero handbag crafted from patchworked leather in denim-inspired hues, while a graphic slogan T-shirt commemorates the collaboration.The accompanying campaign was photographed at London's V&A East Storehouse, where the new pieces appear alongside archival Chalayan designs, including his 2011 Tulle Dress and the Haiku Dress from the Sakoko SS11 collection. Coinciding with the release is Reference: Hussein Chalayan, a limited-edition book of 1,000 copies, editorially directed by Charlene Prempeh and featuring archival imagery, illustrations and essays examining the designer's creative legacy.The Acne Studios x Hussein Chalayan collection will be available online and at select Acne Studios boutiques worldwide, including locations in Beijing, Shanghai, Tokyo, Paris, Stockholm, London, New York and Los Angeles. The accompanying publication will also be available through selected retailers and partners globally.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
